Daily Briefing — Wednesday, May 13 2026

Enterprise AI governance emerges as critical differentiator as organizations move from experimentation to operationalization.

AI & Technology

#1 — ServiceNow Knowledge 2026 Reveals Enterprise AI Operating Model Shift Toward Governed Execution — CPrime / ServiceNow Knowledge 2026

★ Directly addresses Cristiano's governance and orchestration priorities—ServiceNow Knowledge 2026 identified governance as the defining enterprise AI theme, with emphasis on runtime governance, multi-LLM environments, and orchestration strategy essential for scaling agentic systems.

ServiceNow Knowledge 2026 established governance as the mechanism enabling trust and scalability in enterprise AI, not bureaucratic overhead. The conference highlighted that agentic AI changes the risk profile of adoption, requiring continuous assurance across build and run-time environments. Organizations increasingly need orchestration layers that stabilize work across changing AI ecosystems while applying governance consistently.

#2 — Data Innovation Summit 2026: Enterprise AI Shifting From Experimentation to Operationalization — Hyperight

★ Validates Cristiano's strategic positioning on enterprise transformation—DIS 2026 emphasized that the next AI challenge is organizational, not purely technical, and that success depends on workflow integration, governance clarity, and operational ownership structures.

Data Innovation Summit 2026 revealed a decisive market maturity shift: enterprises are exhausted by innovation theater disconnected from operational outcomes. Governance has moved beyond theoretical ethics into operational territory—AI inventory systems, explainability, regulatory readiness, and organizational accountability. The market is transitioning from experimentation into operationalization, with success now defined by measurable business value, not deployment novelty.

Financial Services Technology

#1 — KPMG Global AI in Finance Report 2026: Agentic AI Separates Leaders From Rest by 32 Percentage Points — KPMG

★ Directly relevant to R+ product strategy—KPMG's March 2026 survey of 1,013 finance leaders shows agentic AI adoption in judgment-heavy workflows (decision-making, forecasting) delivers measurable ROI, with organizations using agentic AI outperforming peers by 32 percentage points on decision quality and speed.

More than three-quarters of organizations are leveraging AI in financial planning, reporting and commercial analysis, and 71 percent report it is meeting or exceeding ROI expectations. AI in finance is producing the strongest gains in judgment-heavy work, not transactional automation, with decision-making quality (70 percent), decision-making speed (71 percent) and forecasting accuracy (64 percent) leading the gains, and organizations deploying agentic AI for finance separating from the rest by 32 percentage points on average.
